story.iWant: MCP tools to work seamlessly with Gemini's function calling format
story.soThat: Gemini provider has feature parity with Grok-4 and ChatGPT-5, enabling users to leverage internet search, memory storage, and profile access regardless of which provider is active
story.tasks:
### Task 1: Create Gemini Tool Adapter Module - [ ] 1.1 Create GeminiToolAdapter class with schema conversion methods - [ ] 1.2 Implement convert_openai_to_gemini_schema(openai_tools: list) -> list - [ ] 1.3 Implement convert_gemini_to_openai_call(gemini_call: dict) -> dict - [ ] 1.4 Implement format_tool_result_for_gemini(tool_result: dict) -> dict - [ ] 1.5 Add schema validation with Pydantic models for type safety
### Task 2: Integrate Tool Adapter into GeminiProvider - [ ] 2.1 Import and initialize GeminiToolAdapter in GeminiProvider.__init__() - [ ] 2.2 Update stream_chat_completion() to accept MCP tools parameter - [ ] 2.3 Convert MCP tool schemas to Gemini format before API call - [ ] 2.4 Detect function calls in streaming response chunks - [ ] 2.5 Execute tool calls via existing MCP client - [ ] 2.6 Format tool results and append to conversation context - [ ] 2.7 Continue streaming final LLM response after tool execution
### Task 3: Handle Multi-Turn Tool Calling - [ ] 3.1 CRITICAL: Preserve thought_signature from Gemini responses - [ ] 3.2 Maintain tool call history in conversation context - [ ] 3.3 Implement sequential tool call logic - [ ] 3.4 Add max iterations limit (prevent infinite loops) - [ ] 3.5 Track tool call chain and thought_signatures in Langfuse for debugging
### Task 4: Add Tool Call Event Streaming - [ ] 4.1 Emit tool_call_started SSE event when function call detected - [ ] 4.2 Emit tool_call_completed event with result summary - [ ] 4.3 Emit tool_call_failed event on errors with helpful message - [ ] 4.4 Ensure Telegram bot displays tool activity to user
### Task 5: Error Handling for Tool Calls - [ ] 5.1 Handle MCP server unreachable - [ ] 5.2 Handle tool execution timeout - [ ] 5.3 Handle invalid tool arguments - [ ] 5.4 Handle tool result too large
### Task 6: Integration Tests for Gemini + MCP - [ ] 6.1 Test basic tool calling flow - [ ] 6.2 Test multi-tool sequence - [ ] 6.3 Test tool error handling - [ ] 6.4 Test tool call timeout - [ ] 6.5 Test parallel tool calls (if Gemini supports)
### Task 7: Unit Tests for Tool Adapter - [ ] 7.1 Test OpenAI → Gemini schema conversion - [ ] 7.2 Test Gemini → OpenAI tool call conversion - [ ] 7.3 Test tool result formatting - [ ] 7.4 Test edge cases
### Task 8: Update LLM Client Factory - [ ] 8.1 Pass MCP tool list to GeminiProvider during initialization - [ ] 8.2 Update stream_chat_completion() signature to accept tools parameter - [ ] 8.3 Update all provider implementations to accept tools parameter - [ ] 8.4 Update streaming logic to handle tool call events

story-context.acceptanceCriteria:
### AC#1: MCP Tool Compatibility - All existing MCP tools work with Gemini provider (internet_search, store_memory, retrieve_memories, get_user_profile) - Tool execution produces identical results regardless of provider
### AC#2: Schema Conversion - Tool adapter converts OpenAI tool schema → Gemini function_declarations format - Conversion handles parameter types, required/optional parameters, nested objects/arrays, enum constraints, descriptions
### AC#3: Streaming Tool Results - Tool results properly formatted for SSE streaming to Telegram - Tool call status events sent during execution (tool_call_started, tool_call_completed, tool_call_failed) - Final response incorporates tool results naturally
### AC#4: Error Handling - Tool call failures handled gracefully (MCP server unreachable, timeout, invalid arguments, result too large) - Langfuse traces capture tool call failures with error metadata
### AC#5: Multi-Tool Sequences - Multiple tool calls in single conversation work correctly - Tool results from previous calls available in context - Sequential dependencies handled properly - Parallel tool calls execute concurrently (if Gemini supports)
### AC#6: Context Integration - Tool results properly incorporated into LLM context for next turn - Context window management preserves tool history - Tool result formatting optimized for Gemini's input format - Token counting includes tool call overhead

doc.title: Epic 9: Multi-LLM Provider Support - Add Gemini 3 Pro

docs.doc: Provides comprehensive context for implementing Gemini tool calling. Includes tool adapter design (OpenAI to Gemini format conversion), function calling API examples with thought_signature preservation, multi-turn tool calling patterns, and error handling strategies.

Defines provider abstraction layer architecture using Strategy + Factory + Facade patterns. GeminiToolAdapter converts OpenAI schema to Gemini function_declarations format. Provider-specific adapters translate native formats while maintaining OpenAI-compatible schema for MCP tools.
Backend service architecture using FastAPI, MCP server communication via Docker exec with stdio transport, and JSON-RPC 2.0 protocol for tool execution.

artifact.reason: Abstract base class defining provider interface contract. Declares stream_chat_completion() method signature with tools parameter that GeminiProvider must implement for tool calling support.
Existing GeminiProvider implementation (Story 9.2). Needs to be extended with tool calling support, function call detection in streaming chunks, and tool result formatting.
Reference implementation for tool calling with Grok-4. Shows existing pattern for MCP tool integration and streaming tool events.

Existing MCP client for tool execution via JSON-RPC 2.0. Provides call_tool() method that GeminiProvider will use to execute converted tool calls. Includes error handling patterns (MCPNetworkError, MCPToolError).
Factory pattern implementation for provider instantiation. Needs updates to pass MCP tool list to GeminiProvider and handle tool call events in streaming logic.

constraints.constraint: Thought Signature Preservation: Gemini 3 requires thought_signature from previous responses to be included in follow-up requests for function calling. Missing signatures cause 400 errors. SDK auto-handles, but must be verified in implementation.
All existing MCP tools must work unchanged with Gemini provider (internet_search, store_memory, retrieve_memories, get_user_profile).
Gemini tool calling behavior must match Grok-4/ChatGPT-5. Same prompts should trigger same tools with identical results.
Tool execution latency must be <5 seconds (p95) per Story 2.4 requirement.
Graceful degradation when tools fail. MCP server unreachable should return user-friendly error, not crash.
All tool calls must be traced in Langfuse with full metadata (tool name, arguments, results, errors, duration).
80%+ code coverage for tool adapter module. Integration tests must cover all MCP tools with Gemini.
Tool adapter must preserve round-trip conversion (OpenAI → Gemini → OpenAI) without data loss.

interface.name: BaseProvider.stream_chat_completion
interface.signature: async def stream_chat_completion(messages: List[Dict], tools: Optional[List[Dict]] = None) -> AsyncGenerator[Dict, None]

interfaces.interface: Abstract method that GeminiProvider implements. Must accept tools parameter (OpenAI format) and yield streaming events including tool call events (tool_call_started, tool_call_completed, tool_call_failed).

interface.name: MCPClient.call_tool
interface.signature: async def call_tool(tool_name: str, arguments: dict) -> dict

interfaces.interface: Executes MCP tool via JSON-RPC 2.0. GeminiProvider calls this after converting Gemini function call to OpenAI format. Raises MCPNetworkError if server unreachable, MCPToolError if execution fails.

interface.name: MCPClient.list_tools
interface.signature: async def list_tools(use_cache: bool = True) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]

interfaces.interface: Fetches available MCP tools with schemas. Returns list of tools with 'name', 'description', 'inputSchema' in OpenAI format. GeminiToolAdapter converts these to Gemini function_declarations.

Gemini SDK function calling API. Accepts tools in function_declarations format. Returns chunks with function_call in candidates[0].content.parts[0]. Requires thought_signature preservation for multi-turn.

tests.standards: Testing framework: pytest with pytest-asyncio for async support. Unit tests use mocking (unittest.mock) for external dependencies. Integration tests use real MCP server in Docker. Code coverage target: 80%+ for new modules. Test file naming: test_{module_name}.py in tests/unit/ or tests/integration/.
tests.locations: - backend/tests/unit/ - Unit tests with mocked dependencies - backend/tests/integration/ - End-to-end tests with real MCP server - Test files: test_gemini_tool_adapter.py, test_gemini_mcp.py

ideas.test: Test all existing MCP tools (internet_search, store_memory, retrieve_memories, get_user_profile) work with GeminiProvider. Assert tool execution produces identical results regardless of provider (Grok, ChatGPT, Gemini).

Test OpenAI → Gemini schema conversion with internet_search tool. Verify parameter types (string→STRING), required fields, nested objects, enum constraints. Assert round-trip conversion preserves all schema information.

Test tool call SSE events (tool_call_started, tool_call_completed) are emitted during Gemini tool execution. Verify Telegram bot receives status updates. Assert final LLM response incorporates tool results naturally.

Test tool failures: Mock MCP server unreachable (assert graceful error), tool timeout (assert retry with exponential backoff), invalid arguments (assert validation error to LLM). Verify Langfuse captures error metadata.
Test sequential tool calls: retrieve_memories → internet_search → store_memory. Assert tool results available in context for subsequent calls. Verify thought_signature preserved across iterations.
Test tool results appended to conversation context properly. Assert token counting includes tool call overhead. Verify context window management preserves tool history without exceeding limits.
